Modified Treatment Policy Constructors for Continuous Exposures

Source: R/estimands.R
shift.Rd

Define causal Modified Treatment Policies (MTPs) for continuous treatments following the Longitudinal Modified Treatment Policy (LMTP) framework (Díaz, Williams, Hoffman, & Schenck, 2021).

Usage

shift(delta)

scale_tx(factor)

Arguments

delta

Numeric scalar specifying the additive shift applied to observed treatment values.

factor

Strictly positive numeric scalar specifying the multiplicative scaling factor applied to observed treatment values.

Value

An S3 policy object inheriting from "tmle_policy" ("tmle_shift" or "tmle_scale").

Details

Unlike static binary interventions ("treat everyone vs. treat no one"), continuous exposures often violate positivity if we try to force every individual to the exact same dose. Modified Treatment Policies avoid extrapolation by shifting each person's observed exposure realistically:

  • shift(delta) defines an additive shift \(d(a, w) = a + \delta\) (e.g., increasing daily exercise by +15 minutes or reducing dose by -1 unit).

  • scale_tx(factor) defines a multiplicative policy \(d(a, w) = a \cdot \text{factor}\) (e.g., reducing exposure by 10%).

tidytmle estimates the post-intervention density ratio \(g_d(a \mid w) / g(a \mid w)\) nonparametrically via stacked cross-validated classification without parametric normality assumptions.

References

Díaz, I., Williams, N., Hoffman, K. L., & Schenck, E. J. (2021). Nonparametric causal effects based on longitudinal modified treatment policies. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 118(542), 846–857.

Examples

spec_shift <- tmle_spec(
  outcome = y,
  treatment = dose,
  covariates = c(age, bmi),
  estimand = shift(1.0)
)

spec_scale <- tmle_spec(
  outcome = y,
  treatment = dose,
  covariates = c(age, bmi),
  estimand = scale_tx(0.9)
)
